Short title

THE PENDING PROCEEDINGS (INDIAN COURTS)
THE PENDING PROCEEDINGS (INDIAN COURTS)
ACT, 1952.
ACT No. LIV OF 1952
[For Statement of objects and ,reasons, see Gaz. of P. 1952,
Pt. IX, p.8.]
[14th
December, 1952]
An Act to render ineffective certain decrees and orders
passed by courts in India against a Government in Pakistan and to provide an
alternative remedy to persons who have secured such decrees or orders.
1. Short title. This Act
may be called the Pending Proceedings (Indian Courts) Act, 1952,

Definition

December, 1952]
An Act to render ineffective certain decrees and orders
passed by courts in India against a Government in Pakistan and to provide an
alternative remedy to persons who have secured such decrees or orders.
2. Definition. In this Act
the expression "decree to which this Act applies" means any such
judgment, decree or order as is refer red to in‑
(i) paragraph (3) of Article 4 of the
Indian Indepen dence (Legal Proceedings) Order, 1947, or O. 11 of 1947.
(ii) paragraph
(4) or paragraph (6) of Article 13 of the High Courts (Bengal) Order, 1947, or
O. 4 of 1947.
(iii) paragraph
(5) or paragraph (6) of Article 13 of the High Courts (Punjab) Order, 1947, O.
5 of 1947.
which has been passed by a court
in India and which imposes any liability or obligation on a Government in
Pakistan.

Certain Indian decrees not to be given effect to in Pakistan

3. Certain Indian decrees not
to be given effect to in Pakistan. Notwithstanding anything contained in
any of the Orders referred to in section 2, no decree to which this Act applies
shall be given effect to by any court or authority in Pakistan in so far as
such decree imposes any liability or obliga tion on any Government in Pakistan.

Right of holder of a decree to which this Act applies to institute fresh proceedings in Pakistan

ACT, 1952.
ACT No. LIV OF 1952

[14th
December, 1952]
An Act to render ineffective certain decrees and orders
passed by courts in India against a Government in Pakistan and to provide an
alternative remedy to persons who have secured such decrees or orders.
4. Right of holder of a decree
to which this Act applies to institute fresh proceedings in Pakistan.
Notwithstanding anything contained in section 3 of the Limitation Act, 1908,
any person in whose favour a decree to which this Act applies has been passed
may, within one year from the commencement of this Act, institute a fresh suit
or other legal proceeding in respect of the cause of action on which such
decree was based, and any suit or other legal proceeding may, notwithstanding
anything contained in section 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, or in
any other law or in any agreement to the contrary relating to the place of
suing, be instituted in any court otherwise competent to try it, within the
local limits of whose jurisdiction the person instituting it voluntarily
resides or carries on business or personally works for gain. IX of 1908. V of
1908.

Repeal of Ordinance IX of 1952

5. Repeal of Ordinance IX of
1952.‑(1) The Pending Proceedings (Indian Courts) Ordin ance, 1952,
is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal,
anything done or any action taken in the exercise of any power conferred by or
under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken in the
exercise of the powers conferred by or under this Act, as if this Act were in
force on the day on which such thing was done or such action was taken.
